result.topic_en: Euler applies his general series-to-continued-fraction formula to the cases x=1, y=1, y=2 and y=3, getting continued fractions for expressions involving logarithms. He then says his new method has enriched the theory of continued fractions and begins to introduce a theorem generalizing the continued fraction for 1/(e-1).
result.transcription:
$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{l(1+\sqrt{2})} = 1 + \cfrac{1\cdot2}{1+\cfrac{3\cdot4}{1+\cfrac{5\cdot6}{1+\text{etc.}}}}$
ipsa serie infinita existente
$\frac{l(1+\sqrt{2})}{\sqrt{2}} = 1 - \frac{2}{3} + \frac{2\cdot4}{3\cdot5} - \frac{2\cdot4\cdot6}{3\cdot5\cdot7} + \frac{2\cdot4\cdot6\cdot8}{3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot9} - \text{etc.}$
Sin autem manente $x = 1$ sumamus $y = 2$, series infinita erit
$\frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{4} + \frac{2\cdot4}{3\cdot5}\cdot\frac{1}{8} - \frac{2\cdot4\cdot6}{3\cdot5\cdot7}\cdot\frac{1}{16} + \text{etc.}$
fractio vero continua haec:
$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{l\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}} = 2 + \cfrac{1\cdot2\cdot2}{4+\cfrac{3\cdot4\cdot2}{6+\cfrac{5\cdot6\cdot2}{8+\text{etc.}}}}$
vnde sequens forma deducitur:
$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2l\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}} = 1 + \cfrac{1}{2+\cfrac{6}{3+\cfrac{15}{4+\cfrac{28}{5+\text{etc.}}}}}$
vbi numeratores sunt numeri trigonales alternatim sumti.
§. 60. Euoluamus adhuc casum quo $x = 1$ et $y = 3$, quoniam irrationalitas hoc modo tolletur; erit autem hoc casu
$\frac{1}{4}l3 = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{9} + \frac{2\cdot4}{3\cdot5}\cdot\frac{1}{27} - \frac{2\cdot4\cdot6}{3\cdot5\cdot7}\cdot\frac{1}{81} + \text{etc.}$
fractio autem continua hinc nata erit
$\frac{4}{l3} = 3 + \cfrac{1\cdot2\cdot3}{7+\cfrac{3\cdot4\cdot3}{11+\cfrac{5\cdot6\cdot3}{15+\cfrac{7\cdot8\cdot3}{19+\text{etc.}}}}}$
§. 61. Quoniam igitur hic nouam plane methodum aperui, series quascunque infinitas in fractiones continuas transformandi, merito equidem mihi videor doctrinam fractionum continuarum haud mediocriter locupletasse. His igitur tantum subiungam theorema notatu dignissimum, quo supra §42. fractionem
$\cfrac{1}{1+\cfrac{1}{2+\cfrac{2}{3+\cfrac{3}{4+\text{etc.}}}}} = \frac{1}{e-1}$
transformauimus in hanc:
$1+\cfrac{1}{2+\cfrac{2}{3+\cfrac{3}{4+\text{etc.}}}} = \frac{e}{e-1}$
quod multo latius patens ita se habet
Theo-

items.english: where the numerators are the triangular numbers taken alternately.

items.quote: Quoniam igitur hic nouam plane methodum aperui, series quascunque infinitas in fractiones continuas transformandi, merito equidem mihi videor doctrinam fractionum continuarum haud mediocriter locupletasse.
items.english: Since I have here revealed an entirely new method of transforming any infinite series whatever into continued fractions, I think I have rightly enriched the theory of continued fractions not a little.

items.quote: His igitur tantum subiungam theorema notatu dignissimum, quo supra §42. fractionem
